name: tree-code-viewer
title: Tree Code Viewer
description: A two-pane source browser: a collapsible file tree beside a syntax-highlighted code pane. Clicking a file swaps the code, folders expand, and a corner button copies the raw text.
use: Documentation should show a component together with the several files it is built from.
avoid: It needs pre-highlighted HTML handed in, so the highlighter has to run before this renders.
a11y: Tree rows and the copy control are click-only divs with no roles or labels, so nothing here is keyboard reachable. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A bordered two-column frame. The left column lists folders and files with small icons and guide lines, one row shaded for the selection; the right column shows monospace code with coloured keywords and a small copy button in its corner.
behaves: Clicking a folder row expands or collapses it, while clicking a file row moves the selection and fades in that file's code. The copy button writes the raw source to the clipboard and swaps to a double tick for a moment.
customise: A files array with id, name, path, extension, raw text and pre-highlighted HTML drives it; default expansions and copy behaviour stay in the source.
weight: moderate: The viewer itself is light, but the demo pulls in a full syntax highlighter to build the HTML.
demo: A pricing-card example project with pricing-card.tsx, use-billing-cycle.ts, button.tsx, utils.ts and package.json.
issues: Frame 2 highlights a new file while the pane still shows the previous file's code.
Tree rows and the copy button are divs, so the viewer cannot be used from the keyboard.
polishWhy: Crisp two-pane layout and readable highlighting; mouse-only controls are the main flaw.
